analysis: Documentation-only changes. hardware-support.md head 318-340 adds: (1) the cold-load FIFO release (releaseWorkFIFO, awaitReleasedLoads) letting later requests reach fastAdmissionReject while a load runs. The pending-load claims, the gate and eviction still decide every load. A request for an idle resident model can keep a slot a released load would have evicted, so that load fails after acceptance. This is an availability/ordering behavior (T-010/T-029 class) and is opt-out via DARKBLOOM_TTFT_COLD_LOAD_RELEASE=0. (2) PromptPieceTokenStore is per-tokenizer process heap bounded by DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE_MB (default 32 MiB), with no admission claim. inference.md head 1030-1047 documents PromptTokenCache: per-piece token-ID reuse scoped to the prefix-cache scope, ChatTemplateLoopRewrites for Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS, a load-time comparison plus sampled background comparisons that disable reuse on mismatch, and a kill switch. Relevant to T-041/A-001: the in-memory cache holds tokenized plaintext prompt pieces keyed within the coordinator-authored cacheSalt scope. The docs claim reuse never crosses scope, so this adds no cross-account sharing beyond the accepted same-account SEC-035 timing oracle. Tokenization speed differences could add a minor same-scope timing signal. Integration should verify in source (PromptTokenCache.swift, LocalTokenizerBridge) that: the cache key includes the cacheSalt scope; disabled-cache requests (no scope) never populate or read the store; nothing is persisted to disk; and divergence from applyChatTemplate fails toward the unchanged path. The template rewrites could alter rendered prompts and therefore model behavior (T-007 class, correctness rather than confidentiality); the sampled comparisons mitigate this only probabilistically. Source code was not supplied, so no regression is evidenced.
